svg.text: TYPOGRAPHY LOCKED: ALL CAPS · MEDIUM TRACKING · ORIGINAL DARK
Rectangular notch on outer square. Gap on inner ring, aligned to same corner. Both details point the same direction — top-right — doubling down on orientation.
↳ Two details, one direction. The notch declares the corner; the inner gap echoes it. Reads as a very deliberate orientation system — like a compass rose reduced to geometry.
The risk: two details can feel like two ideas. At 32px the gap in the inner ring softens and the notch carries the full load — which actually works.
Rectangular notch anchors the top-right. Inner ring and center dot shift toward bottom-left. Maximum directional tension — the notch pulls one way, the mass pulls the other.
↳ The notch fixes orientation (this is the top-right, this is where pin 1 is); the offset creates gravitational pull in the opposite corner. The mark feels loaded — like it has a center of mass.
Strongest shape in the family. The two details don't fight — they explain each other. This is the one I'd take to a professional mark refinement.
Original chamfer + inner ring gap + offset center of mass. Maximum expression. Testing whether three details read as a system or collapse into noise.
↳ Surprisingly coherent. The chamfer, gap, and offset all pull toward the same top-right / bottom-left axis — it reads as a single diagonal gesture, not three separate ideas.
The risk is that it's overworked. At 32px the gap and offset remain visible but the chamfer is indistinguishable from the notch. Could simplify to Hybrid B at small sizes.
Original through all three hybrids, equal scale, light and dark. This is the full family to date.
Mark: Hybrid B — Pin-1 Notch outer + Offset inner ring and center.
Type: ALL CAPS · Helvetica Neue 700 · 3px tracking.
Sub-brand: "PROSTEC" constant, lowercase suffix (sleep / cove / climate / light).
Hardware variant: Hybrid A (notch + C-ring) at heavy weight for physical emboss/silkscreen.
Primary colour: #111111. No gradients. No second colour required at launch.
